## Functional acceptance covered by completed checks

- [x] Grid previews use the longest selected record as one shared X/Y genomic domain.
- [x] The longest selected self plot retains the complete available cell extent, while
      a shorter self plot occupies only its proportional lower-left square and leaves
      unsupported top and right space blank.
- [x] Pairwise cells use the column sequence's proportional X extent and the row
      sequence's proportional Y extent, keeping their footprints aligned with the
      corresponding self plots.
- [x] The reciprocal preview remains transposed under the shared scale, preserving the
      displayed column-as-X and row-as-Y ordering.
- [x] A medium-by-short pair where neither sequence defines the grid maximum retains
      its independent 75% X and 50% Y extents, covering the pair-domain-to-grid-domain
      conversion in addition to longest-by-shortest comparisons.
- [x] Dragging an axis label preserves the completed canvas bytes and proportional
      extents and sends no additional worker preparation request.
- [x] Visual inspection of the browser capture confirmed lower-left anchoring and the
      expected 100%, 75%, and 50% row and column extents.

## Local toolchain note

On the macOS validation host, the pinned Rust 1.98.0 toolchain's `rust-lld` runtime
path was not discoverable automatically. The pinned binary paths and a temporary linker
wrapper supplied that runtime path. Restricted `wasm-pack` execution also required one
approved download of its pinned `wasm-bindgen` helper. These were local toolchain
environment constraints rather than source failures.

## Release finalization note

The inherited source workspace has no Git metadata. Commit-derived source packaging,
annotated tagging, publication, deployment, and upload therefore remain intentionally
pending even after the local release gates complete.
